official_title: Cholesterol Reduction With Evolocumab and Coronary MicrovascuLar Function and Coronary Flow: The CHORAL Flow Study

primary_outcomes.measure: Maximal coronary flow velocity changes from baseline to 12 weeks
primary_outcomes.time_frame: Measured at baseline and after 12 weeks of therapy

brief_summary: CHORAL Flow is a randomised, double blinded, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of evolocumab on coronary flow at 12 weeks.

inclusion.text: willing to provide consent: Provide written (signed and dated) informed consent and be capable of understanding the study and co-operating with treatment and follow-up.
inclusion.group: Patients aged between 18 and 80 years, with a clinical indication for coronary angiography and

inclusion.text: raised levels of fasting (>9h) LDL-cholesterol (≥2mmol/L) either on optimal statin therapy (90% of overall sample) or intolerants to statins (restricted to 10% of overall sample). Optimal statin therapy will be defined as at least 4 weeks of atorvastatin 40mg or more, with no change in statin dose during this period.
inclusion.group: Patients aged between 18 and 80 years, with a clinical indication for coronary angiography and

inclusion.text: at least one other risk factor for vascular disease or established vascular disease.
inclusion.group: Patients aged between 18 and 80 years, with a clinical indication for coronary angiography and

inclusion.text: willing and able to use a highly effective method of contraception from screening until 15 weeks after the last dose of IP if a woman of childbearing potential.
inclusion.group: Patients aged between 18 and 80 years, with a clinical indication for coronary angiography and

exclusion.text: Patients unable or unwilling to provide written informed consent;
Patients unable to undergo cardiac catheterisation;

Patients with contraindication to adenosine (severe asthma, second or third degree atrioventricular block, heart rate lower than 40/min at rest, previous formal diagnosis of long QT syndrome, acute decompensated heart failure, severe hypotension, advanced (stage IV) or decompensated chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD);
Uncontrolled hypertension (systolic BP >180mmHg or DBP >110mmHg, despite ongoing therapy);
Clinical heart failure NYHA class III/IV or Ejection Fraction on imaging modality (Echo, MRI) <40%;
Recent (last 12 months) clinically significant cerebrovascular event (including ischaemic or haemorrhagic events);
Advanced liver disease, defined as aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) > 3x ULN
Currently or within last 3 months enrolled on another CTIMP;
Known allergy to evolocumab or incipients;
Women of childbearing potential who are unwilling or unable to use a highly effective method of contraception from screening until 15 weeks after the last dose of IP.
Subject is pregnant or breast feeding or planning to become pregnant or to breastfeed during screening, during treatment with IP and/ or within 15 weeks after the end of treatment with IP.
